subject: Accounting
title: Tesco's Profit Overstatement
description: A short lesson to help you apply Tesco's Profit Overstatement.

hook.text: Tesco, Britain's largest retailer, overstated profits by £263 million in 2014.

buildup.text: Executives booked supplier rebates early and delayed recording costs to inflate earnings.

discovery.text: A whistleblower alerted the board. An investigation confirmed the profit overstatement.

twist.text: The company had been under intense pressure from discount competitors eating its market share.

climax.text: Tesco paid a £129 million fine. Three executives were charged with fraud.

punchline.text: Pressure to perform doesn't justify fraud.

quiz.question: How did Tesco overstate its profits?
options: Booking supplier rebates early and delaying costs

details.summary: Tesco, Britain's largest retailer, overstated its profits by £326 million in 2014 by booking supplier rebates too early and deferring costs. This topic covers how the overstatement was discovered, the SFO investigation, and the impact on Tesco's reputation.
details.whyItMatters: Tesco shows that accounting manipulation isn't limited to exotic financial instruments. Even straightforward retail operations can be manipulated through timing of revenue and expense recognition.
takeaways: Tesco booked supplier rebate income before it was earned and deferred recognizing known costs
A whistleblower triggered an internal investigation that revealed the £326 million overstatement
Three executives were charged with fraud though ultimately acquitted at trial

faq.question: How did Tesco overstate its profits?
faq.answer: Tesco booked income from supplier rebates and promotional payments before the conditions for earning them were met, while simultaneously delaying recognition of known costs. This pulled future income into the current period and pushed current costs into the future.

faq.question: What happened after the Tesco overstatement was discovered?
faq.answer: Tesco's stock price dropped sharply, wiping out billions in market value. The Serious Fraud Office charged three executives, though they were acquitted. Tesco paid a £129 million fine in a deferred prosecution agreement and underwent a major corporate overhaul.
